title: docs(plugin-detail): retire the stale strip-mode narration in two spec-parity tests
body:
Fixes #4918

Comment-only. **No assertion changed meaning** — every added and removed line in this diff is a `//` comment (proof below).

Two `plugin-detail` spec-parity blocks narrated strip mode as a present-tense fact about the installed `@objectstack/spec`. The props schemas were closed upstream, so an undeclared top-level key now draws a named `unrecognized_keys` refusal. Because no assertion depended on the sentence, it survived the pin bump reading as current — the exact shape that nearly made a seat implement a no-op once before.

Disposition follows the sibling that already models it, `recordHighlightsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts` (PR #4671): state the pin-independent verdict, note that the contract expresses it two ways depending on the installed pin, and point at `specRefusesUnknownTopLevelKeys` as the behavioural probe instead of narrating a mode as fact.

## Premise re-measured on today's `origin/main`

Both blocks still narrated strip mode at base `1939c9610`, so `premise_still_valid: true` for both halves. Neither had been corrected by anything in flight.

## Before / after

**`packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/recordRelatedListInputs.spec-parity.test.ts`** (~line 100)

Before:
```
    // A KEY-reachability claim, so the criterion is that the key SURVIVES the
    // parse rather than merely that the parse succeeds. `RecordRelatedListProps`
    // is a strip-mode `z.object`: an UNDECLARED key also parses green, it is just
    // silently gone from `data` afterwards — which is exactly how this gap stayed
    // invisible for as long as it did.
```

After:
```
    // A KEY-reachability claim, so the criterion is that the key SURVIVES the
    // parse rather than merely that the parse succeeds. The verdict behind that
    // choice holds on every pin — an UNDECLARED top-level key is not an authoring
    // surface — but the contract states it two ways depending on the installed
    // `@objectstack/spec`: the closed props schemas refuse it with a named
    // `unrecognized_keys`, while the older strip-mode `z.object`s parsed it green
    // and dropped it from `data` in silence, which is exactly how this gap stayed
    // invisible for as long as it did. Key survival is the criterion that reads
    // the same either way; `success === true` does not, because on a stripping
    // pin an undeclared key gets that too. For the behavioural probe of which way
    // the installed pin says it, see `specRefusesUnknownTopLevelKeys` in the
    // sibling `recordHighlightsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts` — strictness is per
    // schema, so that probe is the shape to copy, not evidence about this one.
```

**`packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/recordDetailsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts`** (~line 278)

Before:
```
    // A KEY-reachability claim, so the criterion is that the key SURVIVES the
    // parse. These props schemas are strip-mode `z.object`s: an undeclared key
    // is dropped from `data` with no error at all, which is exactly why the gap
    // was silent — so "it is still there afterwards" is the proof, not
    // `success === true` (which an undeclared key also gets).
```

After:
```
    // A KEY-reachability claim, so the criterion is that the key SURVIVES the
    // parse. The verdict behind that choice is the same on every pin — an
    // undeclared top-level key is not an authoring surface — while the contract
    // states it two ways depending on the installed `@objectstack/spec`: the
    // closed props schemas refuse it with a named `unrecognized_keys` (the
    // top-level twin of `specRefusesUnknownSectionKeys` above), where the older
    // strip-mode `z.object`s dropped it from `data` with no error at all, which
    // is exactly why the gap was silent. So "it is still there afterwards" is the
    // proof on both, and `success === true` is not — on a stripping pin an
    // undeclared key gets that too. Probed behaviourally rather than off a
    // version string: `specRefusesUnknownTopLevelKeys` in the sibling
    // `recordHighlightsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts` models the shape, and
    // strictness is per schema, so it is the pattern rather than a reading of
    // this one.
```

This also settles the card's second observation — `recordDetailsInputs` disagreeing with itself. Its section-key block was already pin-aware and asserts `unrecognized_keys`; its top-level block forty lines down still narrated strip mode. The two now read consistently, and the top-level block names the section-level probe as its twin.

No version literal was written into the new prose: it says "the installed pin", never a number.

## The claim is measured, not asserted

Prose-only, so **no ablation is available** — there is no assertion whose removal could turn anything red, which is precisely why the stale sentence survived. Stating that plainly rather than staging a decorative reverse-verification.

What stands in for it: the new prose makes a behavioural claim, so that claim was probed against the installed pin — an undeclared top-level key fed to each props schema, with a declared-key control that must parse green.

```
=== RecordRelatedListProps (file A, ~line 100) ===
  control(declared keys only).success = true
  probe(+undeclared top-level key).success = false
  MODE = strict; issue codes = ["unrecognized_keys"]
  unrecognized_keys names = ["__objectui_4918_probe__"]

=== RecordDetailsProps (file B, ~line 278) ===
  control(declared keys only).success = true
  probe(+undeclared top-level key).success = false
  MODE = strict; issue codes = ["unrecognized_keys"]
  unrecognized_keys names = ["__objectui_4918_probe__"]
```

The control is the load-bearing half: a bare "it failed" would also be satisfied by a rejection of the declared keys, which is the half that must stay valid. Both controls parse green, and the refusal names the probe key and only the probe key.

## No assertion moved

```
$ git diff -U0 | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---)' | grep -vE '^[+-][[:space:]]*//'
(none — every changed line is a // comment)

 .../recordRelatedListInputs.spec-parity.test.ts | 16 ++++++++++++----
 2 files changed, 25 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)
```

## Verification

All legs below ran against the final commit, `0c28940e6`. Heavy legs went through the shared verify lock.

    scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts --maxWorkers=2

      Tests  41 passed (41)

$ pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build

Exit codes were captured before any pipe (`cmd > out 2>&1; EXIT=$?; tail out`), and each line quoted above is the gate's own printed verdict, not a bare `$?`.

The changeset is empty-frontmatter: comment-only, releases nothing.

### Declared lint narrowing

Linted the changed files rather than sweeping the repo (the whole-repo sweep is CI's run, and holding the shared lock for it would starve the queue). The narrowing is measured, with all three pieces:

1. **Population read from eslint's own config**, not guessed: of the 3 changed files, eslint reports the `.changeset/*.md` as `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied` — it is outside the linted population by the config's own account. The 2 `.ts` files are in it.
2. **Count read from `--format json`**: 3 entries returned, 2 linted, **0 errors / 0 warnings** on both, `ESLINT_EXIT=0`.
3. **Invariance for untouched files**: this repo's `eslint.config.js` sets no `project` / `projectService`, so linting is **not type-aware** — a comment-only edit inside two test files cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. Confirmed by grep against the config.

Gate re-derivation: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is a framework-repo tool with no objectui counterpart, so the set was re-derived by hand over the actual changed paths — which added `check-changeset-fixed` and `check-spec-symbol-derivation` (the new prose names spec export symbols) beyond the dispatched list. Both green above.

## One judgement call left open for the PM

The card and the triage comment both flag it: should the `recordDetailsInputs` top-level block also **grow** a pin-aware probe (`specRefusesUnknownTopLevelKeys`), rather than only losing the stale sentence? Triage leaned yes. This dispatch was scoped prose-only with an explicit bar on assertion changes, so it is **not** done here and is reported rather than silently absorbed — a prose card quietly growing an assertion is the shape this repo keeps paying for.

Worth knowing for that decision: neither of these two files can borrow the sibling's probe as *evidence*. Strictness is per schema — `recordDetailsInputs` says so itself at its section-level probe — so a real top-level probe here would have to be a new constant per file, roughly the four lines the sibling spends. The new prose is written to stay correct either way: it names the sibling's probe as the shape to copy, not as a reading of these schemas.
